reason: Selected diagnostic reflection comparisons and ablations support tested diagnosis-plus-correction, while limiting causal claims about memory contamination.

candidates.title: Diagnose the failing agent and step before generating reflections
candidates.rule: For task-oriented multi-agent workflows, compare diagnosis-plus-counterfactual-correction followed by targeted reflection with undiagnosed reflection over the entire failed run.
candidates.passage: removing both diagnosis and correction submodules causes the largest degradation
candidates.finding: The complete DoCtOR loop and its ablations favor diagnosis and correction; prompt-based Reflexion gains are modest with GPT-4o and larger for GPT-3.5 on two tasks. Failure localization is imperfect, especially on held-out datasets.
models: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4o prompt-based transfer experiments
PPO-trained DoCtOR reflector; exact main backbone not established in inspected sections
candidates.conditions: Task success must be observable; evaluations sample one hundred tasks per dataset. Diagnosis identifies a decisive agent/step before generating corrected feedback.
candidates.limitations: Combined-component evidence does not isolate every targeting or memory-contamination mechanism. Step attribution accuracy falls to 20–38% on the reported held-out sets. Small teams and English tasks limit transfer.
candidates.validation_test: Compare full, diagnosis-only and undiagnosed reflection at matched budget; validate assigned failure causes with counterfactual replays and measure downstream success plus false lessons stored.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
